matches.gold_text: Proposals must be received by the City by 3:00 p.m. PT on September 17, 2024.
Proposals must not be submitted by fax.
The vendor must offer ERP software and services that satisfy all of the City's functional and technical requirements.
The preferred vendor has experience successfully implementing the proposed solutions for cities of similar size and scope of services.
Any best-of-breed Human Capital Management solution offered must be able to integrate with the selected ERP system.
A vendor responding with a best-of-breed solution must complete the Section 6 Requirements template for the relevant functionality and submit it per the Section 5 instructions.
The vendor must provide an integrated ERP solution that includes the modules and functionality defined in the Requirements document.
The replacement ERP solution is to be implemented in phases or as recommended by the selected vendor and approved by the City.
Vendors invited to demonstrate their product should be prepared to discuss the application's best practices and its ability to adapt to user preferences.
The City's estimated implementation window runs from March 2025 through January 2027.
All modules in scope must go live by January 1, 2027.
Finalist vendors must follow the City's pre-defined script during their software demonstrations.
The proposal must be one electronic PDF copy, in the order defined in the response format table, not exceeding 100 total pages excluding sample contracts.
The response must include one completed copy of the Requirements document in MS Word format, with the Word format unmodified.
Proposals should be emailed to the City contact at Thuch.Mam@FederalWayWA.gov.
All data, materials and documentation originated and prepared for the City under this solicitation belong to the City.
Vendor questions about the RFP may be submitted by email to the City contact by August 28, 2024, 3:00 p.m. PT.
Vendor responses should include the sections outlined in the Proposal Response Format; deviation may lead to the response being deemed non-responsive and disqualified.
Marketing literature should not be included in the proposal.
The proposal must begin with a cover letter that is an executive summary of the proposed software and services, limited to two pages.
The vendor must complete the Pricing Summary from Exhibit A, indicating costs for software and implementation services.
Pricing must be comprehensive, including all taxes and available discounts.
Pricing must remain valid for 180 days from the response date.
The vendor must price the software for the user counts defined in the RFP.
The vendor must provide a separate pricing sheet for each deployment option offered (SaaS or on-premises).
Implementation pricing must include all costs required for go-live, including software deployment, data conversion, system configuration, report development, testing and training.
The vendor must price ongoing license and maintenance for Years 1-10.
Financials software must be priced for 130 named users and 85 concurrent users.
Human Capital Management software must be priced for 400 FTEs and 744 W2s.

The proposal must include an implementation overview covering methodology, sample project plan, City and vendor resources, process improvement, change management, data conversion, testing, training and report development.
The proposal must include an overview of support services offered, including hours, response times, support tiers, post go-live services, backup and disaster recovery.
The proposal must include a technology overview covering architecture and deployment options, data centers, hardware, mobile, remote access, integration tools and software updates.
The proposal must include a security overview covering the security model, standards, SSO/SAML administration, multi-factor authentication and breach response.
The vendor must provide references from three current and two prior customers for the proposed software, using the Exhibit B forms.
Preference is for references from Washington State public sector clients.
The vendor must disclose any contract terminations or legal actions with customers in the past five years, describing each situation with the contracting party's name and address.
The proposal must include sample contract documents such as a statement of work, license agreement, maintenance or support agreements and service level agreements.
The vendor must document any exceptions it has to the RFP content.
The vendor's Requirements responses will be incorporated into the signed contract.
The vendor must provide a rating and a comment for every item in the Requirements document; blank responses may cause rejection.
The vendor must not include hyperlinks in the Requirements document.
The vendor must not modify the format, font or numbering of the Requirements section or insert page breaks.
Requirement comments must give a substantive explanation; generic comments such as "Standard Functionality" are unacceptable.
Each line-item response in the Requirements document must be limited to 100 words.
The vendor must provide a certification of insurance before commencing any work.
An underwriter's endorsement with additional insured verbiage is required, and the surety must be admitted in the State of Washington.

The ERP solution must replace the City's Eden financial modules: General Ledger, Purchasing, Contract Management, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Project and Grant Accounting, and Capital Assets.
The ERP solution must replace the City's Eden Human Resources, Time and Attendance, and Payroll modules, as part of the ERP suite or integrated with it.
The ERP solution must replace the Quadrant cashiering system, as part of the ERP suite or integrated with it.
The ERP solution must replace the Excel-based budget process, as part of the ERP suite or integrated with it.
The ERP solution must replace the Excel-based preparation of the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR), as part of the ERP suite or integrated with it.

The ERP solution must integrate with the retained systems NeoGov (recruiting), Power Time (police scheduling, time and attendance), Amanda and MBC.com (permitting, planning, land management), RecTrac (parks and recreation) and Class (Dumas Bay Conference Center).
Integration of the ERP solution with OpenGov (constituent transparency) and SharePoint (document management) is under review.
Enterprise asset management and fleet management, currently Excel shadow systems, are under review for inclusion in scope; their integration is to be determined.

verdicts.text: Vendor proposals must be received by the City of Federal Way no later than September 17, 2024 at 3:00 p.m. PT.
Late submissions of responses will not be considered.
Responses may not be submitted by fax.
The Vendor must provide ERP software and services that satisfy all of the City's functional and technical requirements.
The preferred Vendor should have experience successfully implementing the proposed solutions for cities of similar size and scope of services.
A Vendor submitting a best-of-breed Human Capital Management solution must demonstrate that the solution can integrate with the selected ERP system.
Submission of a proposal constitutes the Vendor's acknowledgment and acceptance of all terms and conditions contained in the RFP and all its exhibits and attachments.
The Vendor must deliver an integrated ERP solution that includes the modules and functionality defined in the Requirements document provided with this RFP.
The Vendor must implement the replacement ERP solution using a phased approach, or using an alternative approach recommended by the selected Vendor and approved by the City.
Vendors invited to demonstrate their product must be prepared to discuss the application's best practices and the system's ability to adapt to user preferences.
Vendor questions on the RFP must be submitted by August 28, 2024.
The vendor must be available to present software demos in December 2024.
The vendor must be available for due diligence review in January 2025.
The vendor must be available for contract negotiations beginning January 2025.
Implementation must be scheduled to run from March 2025 through January 2027.
The vendor's proposal must demonstrate that all modules required by the City are offered, as scored under the Software evaluation criterion.
The vendor's solution must meet the City's functional and technical requirements in depth of functionality.
The vendor's platform, database and accessibility approach must adhere to the City's IT strategy.
The vendor must demonstrate integration experience and the integration tools it offers.
The vendor must demonstrate organizational strength and viability and vision as an organization.
The vendor must demonstrate experience working with government entities.
The proposal must present a defined and proven implementation methodology.
The proposal must include a proposed implementation timeline and staffing plan.
All modules in scope must go live by January 1, 2027.
The proposal must be submitted initially on the most favorable terms available, since the City may award based solely on the submitted information without further discussion.
Vendors must present their functional and technical product demos to the City according to a pre-defined script.
Vendors must be able to successfully demonstrate the product's ability to meet the City's functional and technical requirements during the demo.
Vendors must be prepared to provide additional information, interviews, follow-up demonstrations or other clarification of proposal information if the City requests it.
Proposals must be prepared simply and economically, providing straightforward, concise descriptions of the Vendor's ability to satisfy the City's functional and technical needs.
Ownership of all data, materials, and documentation originated and prepared for the City pursuant to this solicitation will belong to the City.
Proposals must be emailed to Thuch.Mam@FederalWayWA.gov.
The official submission time of an electronic proposal is the time marked by Outlook in the City staff's email inbox.
The response must include one electronic PDF copy of the entire RFP proposal, ordered as defined in the submission table, not exceeding 100 total pages excluding sample contracts provided.
The response must include one completed copy of the Requirements document in MS Word format.
Vendor proposals should include the sections outlined in the Proposal Response Format.
Proposals that deviate from the requested format may be classified as non-responsive and disqualified.
Marketing literature must not be included in the vendor's proposal.
The proposal must include a Cover Letter that is an executive summary letter of the proposed software and services for the scope of work defined in the RFP, limited to two pages.
The bidder must complete the Requirements document provided as a separate Word document and follow the instructions in Section 6 of the RFP.
Each requirement in the Requirements document must carry a rating and a comment describing how the function is met with the software.
The completed Requirements document must be submitted as Section 2 of the proposal.
The bidder must complete the Pricing Summary from Exhibit A of the RFP, indicating costs for software and implementation services.
Pricing must be comprehensive, including all taxes and available discounts.
Pricing must be valid for 180 days from the response date.
Pricing must include the cost of software for the user counts defined in the RFP, with one sheet for each deployment option if applicable (SaaS or on-premises).

Pricing must include all implementation services costs required for go live, including but not limited to software deployment, data conversion, system configuration, report development, testing, and training.
Pricing must include the cost of ongoing maintenance for Years 1-10.
The proposal must describe City resources by roles, responsibilities and average time per month.
The proposal must describe vendor resources by roles, responsibilities and average time per month.
The proposal must describe the process improvement strategy through implementation.
The proposal must describe the business change management methodology and tools used.
The proposal must describe the data conversion methodology and recommend data conversion by module, including years and data elements.
The proposal must describe the testing methodology and tools.
The proposal must describe the training methodology and tools.
The proposal must describe the report development approach.
The proposal must provide an overview of support services offered, including support hours.
The proposal must state the guaranteed response time, resources available and escalation process for support.
The proposal must compare baseline support versus premium level support.
The proposal must describe user groups and conferences offered.
The proposal must describe post go-live tools and services.
The proposal must describe the backup strategy and support.
The proposal must describe disaster recovery services covering backup, redundancy and location, distinguishing baseline support from premium level.
The proposal must provide an overview of the system technology, including options for technical architecture such as hosted, on-premises or SaaS.
The proposal must describe data center locations and redundancy.
The proposal must provide hardware specifications.
The proposal must describe mobile hardware and operating system options.
The proposal must describe remote access capabilities and supported technologies.
The proposal must describe software updates, including whether they are scheduled or automatic and the update timeline.
The proposal must provide an overview of the system security model.
The proposal must identify the security standards the system meets.
The proposal must describe security administration capabilities such as SSO and SAML.
The proposal must describe multi-factor authentication support.
The proposal must describe security breach handling, including customer communication, response and cost.
The proposal must provide references using the forms provided in Exhibit B, covering three current and two prior customers for the proposed software.
The references provided should be similar in size and scope to the City's project, with preference for Washington State public sector clients.

The proposal must indicate whether the Vendor has had a contract terminated for convenience, non-performance or any other reason, or has entered into legal action with a customer, at any time during the past five years, describing the situations including the name and address of the contracting party.

The proposal must provide sample contract documents, which may include a Statement of Work, a Perpetual Software License or SaaS License Agreement, Maintenance or Support Agreements, and Service Level Agreements.
Each comment must include a brief explanation of how the item is supported.
The vendor must not provide hyperlinks within the ERP Requirements document.
The vendor must not modify the format, font, numbering, etc. of this section or insert page breaks.
The vendor must use the specified rating scale (4, 3, 2, 0, F) to evaluate each requirement.
When rating an item 3 (third-party software), the vendor must indicate the name of the recommended application.
When rating an item 2 (modification), the vendor must indicate the estimated cost of the modification.
When rating an item F (future release), the vendor must indicate the anticipated release month and year.
Answers such as "Standard Functionality" or similar are not acceptable and do not satisfy the information requirement.
The ERP solution must provide an audit trail with user, date and time stamp throughout all modules, capturing before/after values.

A proposer that discovers an ambiguity, conflict, discrepancy, omission or other error in the RFP or its attachments must immediately notify the City in writing and request modification or clarification.

A proposer that fails to notify the City of a known or reasonably knowable RFP error before the proposal submission date bids at its own risk and, if awarded, is not entitled to additional compensation or time for the error or its later correction.
The proposer is responsible for ensuring it has incorporated all addenda issued by the City.
Failure to acknowledge and incorporate addenda does not relieve the proposer of the responsibility to meet all terms and conditions of the RFP and any subsequent addenda.
The proposer bears all costs of developing its proposal, which are not chargeable to the City.
A vendor may not designate its entire submittal as proprietary.
Proposals that refer to terms and conditions other than the City's terms and conditions may be rejected as non-responsive.
The Vendor must provide a certification of insurance prior to commencement of any work.
An underwriter's endorsement with additional insured verbiage is required, and the surety must be an admitted surety in the State of Washington.
Pricing must be structured to cover the Financials scope sized at 130 named users and 85 concurrent users.
Pricing must be structured to cover the Human Capital Management scope sized at 400 FTEs and 744 W2s.

The pricing template must itemize Year 1 software costs for the listed Financial modules (General Ledger, Budget, Project and Grant Accounting, Purchasing and Contract Management, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Capital Assets, Enterprise Cashiering).
The pricing template must itemize Year 1 software costs for the listed Human Capital Management modules (Human Resources, Time and Attendance, Payroll).
The bidder must state assumptions alongside its software, implementation and maintenance pricing.

The proposal must provide prior customer references, listing for each reference the customer name, number of employees, population, contact name and title, contact telephone and email, software scope, implementation duration, go-live date, and reason for change.

component_records.title: Bid mobilisation, RFP compliance and proposal governance
component_records.description: A bid team is stood up immediately to own the submission end to end: question submission by August 28, 2024, a single electronic PDF of no more than 100 pages emailed to the City's named contact, the completed Requirements document in unmodified MS Word format as Section 2, and a two-page cover letter. The same team tracks addenda, logs any RFP error or ambiguity notified to the City in writing, and confirms acceptance of the City's terms and conditions rather than proposing substitute terms. It also holds the calendar for the December 2024 demos, January 2025 due diligence and January 2025 contract negotiations, and stands ready to supply follow-up information or interviews on request.

component_records.title: Requirements document completion and demo readiness
component_records.description: Every line of the City's ERP Requirements document is answered with a rating from the 4/3/2/0/F scale and a comment of no more than 100 words explaining how the software meets the function, with no blank cells, no hyperlinks and no alteration to the document's format, font, numbering or page breaks. Items rated 3 name the recommended third-party application, items rated 2 carry an estimated modification cost, and items rated F carry an anticipated release month and year. The same content is rehearsed as the on-site demo: we present strictly to the City's Demo Script, demonstrate depth of functionality across all required modules, and discuss best practices and user-preference adaptability.

component_records.title: Integrated ERP software suite (financials and HCM)
component_records.description: A single integrated ERP product is supplied covering the eight required financial modules — General Ledger, Budget, Project and Grant Accounting, Purchasing and Contract Management, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Capital Assets and Enterprise Cashiering — and the three required HCM modules — Human Resources, Time and Attendance and Payroll. The suite provides a system-wide audit trail capturing user, date and time stamp with before/after values in every module, and is delivered as a hosted SaaS subscription with an alternative on-premises option priced separately. Where the City prefers best-of-breed HCM, the same financials core is offered with a certified HCM partner product integrated through published APIs and pre-built connectors.

component_records.title: Phased implementation methodology and schedule to January 2027
component_records.description: A proven, documented implementation methodology is applied in phases: mobilisation and fit-gap (March–June 2025), financials configuration and data conversion (mid 2025), HCM configuration and payroll parallel runs (late 2025 into 2026), integration, report development and testing (2026), then training, cutover and go live for all modules by January 1, 2027, followed by stabilisation. Each phase has defined deliverables, City acceptance gates and a change-control route, so the City can approve or vary the approach. The plan is resourced with named vendor roles and City roles, each with responsibilities and average time per month, and is re-baselined with the City if the City exercises its right to reschedule.

component_records.title: Data conversion, integration and report development
component_records.description: A data conversion methodology is delivered module by module, recommending for each module the years of history and the data elements to be converted, with extract, cleanse, validate, mock-convert and reconcile cycles before each go-live wave. Integration services cover interfaces between the ERP, the HCM solution and City third-party systems using the vendor's integration platform and published APIs, with monitoring and error handling. Report development delivers the City's operational and statutory reports plus a self-service reporting layer, and all converted data, reports and documentation prepared for the City become City property.

component_records.title: Technology, security and hosting architecture
component_records.description: The solution is hosted in the vendor's data centres with stated locations and redundancy, and the proposal sets out the platform, database and accessibility approach so the City can confirm alignment with its IT strategy. The security model is documented with the standards met, SSO/SAML and directory-based administration, multi-factor authentication, role-based access, and breach handling covering customer communication, response and cost. The same section covers hardware specifications, mobile hardware and OS options, remote access technologies, and whether software updates are scheduled or automatic with the update timeline.

component_records.title: Training, change management and process improvement
component_records.description: A training methodology and toolset is delivered covering role-based curricula for financial users and HCM users, train-the-trainer for City power users, sandbox environments and post-go-live refresher sessions. Business change management uses a documented methodology and tools — stakeholder mapping, impact assessment, communications and readiness assessments — and the process improvement strategy is carried through design workshops so the City adopts the vendor's best practices rather than replicating current workarounds. User groups and conferences available to City staff are described as part of the same offer.

component_records.title: Support, maintenance and post-go-live services
component_records.description: Ongoing support is provided from go live for Years 1 through 10, with stated support hours, guaranteed response times, named resources and a documented escalation path, and with baseline and premium support levels compared side by side so the City can choose. Post-go-live tools and services include a hypercare period, a health-check programme, release management for scheduled updates, and backup and disaster recovery covering backup frequency, redundancy and location. The offer is backed by three current and two prior customer references, with preference given to Washington State public sector clients of comparable size and scope.

component_records.title: Pricing, assumptions and commercial submission
component_records.description: The City's Exhibit A Pricing Summary is completed with Year 1 software itemised line by line for each of the eight financial modules and each of the three HCM modules, implementation services priced to go live (deployment, data conversion, configuration, report development, testing, training, integration and travel), and maintenance or subscription for Years 1 through 10. Financials are sized at 130 named and 85 concurrent users and HCM at 400 FTEs and 744 W-2s, with a separate sheet for each deployment option offered. All taxes and available discounts are included, the price is held valid for 180 days, and every figure carries a stated assumption; proposal development costs are borne by the vendor.

component_records.title: Contract, insurance and compliance obligations
component_records.description: A contract and compliance workstream accepts the City's terms and conditions in full, provides sample contract documents (Statement of Work, licence agreement, maintenance/support agreement and service level agreement), and discloses any contract terminated for convenience or non-performance or legal action with a customer in the past five years. Before any work begins the vendor supplies a certificate of insurance with an underwriter's endorsement naming the City as additional insured and a surety admitted in the State of Washington. The workstream also confirms that no contract is effective until City Council approval and that the City may reject any or all proposals.

items.text: The City of Federal Way, Washington, is the issuing body and sole beneficiary of this RFP, seeking proposals from experienced and qualified vendors for ERP software and services.
items.reason: 'Sole beneficiary' is not stated; the source only says the City is seeking proposals.

items.text: The City incorporated in February 1990 and changed from a council-manager to a mayor-council form of government in November 2010.
items.reason: Incorporation in February 1990 and the November 2010 change to mayor-council are both stated.

items.text: The City is a residential and commercial community with an estimated 22,485 people employed within the city limits.
items.reason: Residential and commercial community and 22,485 employed within city limits are stated.

items.text: The City's current environment is described in a scope table that designates which existing solutions are in scope for replacement, but the table's contents are not reproduced in the RFP text.
items.reason: The table's non-reproduction is a fair reading, but the source doesn't say the table designates solutions 'for replacement'; it says 'in scope'.

items.text: The City intends to replace its existing ERP solution and expects process improvement through the new systems, adopting the best practices offered by the selected vendor.
items.reason: Replacement ERP, expected process improvement and adoption of vendor best practices are all stated.

items.text: The City's user base spans 130 named and 85 concurrent financial users, 400 FTEs and 744 W-2s for Human Capital Management.
items.reason: Pricing header lists 130 named, 85 concurrent users, 400 FTEs and 744 W2s.

items.text: The City is open to best-of-breed Human Capital Management vendors in addition to a single integrated ERP, provided those solutions can integrate with the selected ERP system.
items.reason: Open to best-of-breed HCM vendors that can integrate with the selected ERP is stated.

items.text: The City wants to purchase an integrated ERP solution covering the modules and functionality defined in the Requirements document supplied with the RFP.
items.reason: Source states intent to purchase an integrated ERP with modules defined in the Requirements document.

items.text: The City expects the replacement ERP to be implemented using a phased approach, or as recommended by the selected vendor and approved by the City.
items.reason: Phased approach or vendor-recommended approach approved by the City is stated.

items.text: Go-live date conflicts with the implementation window. R018 schedules implementation from March 2025 through January 2027, while R027 and the Implementation scoring criterion require all modules live by January 1, 2027. Read literally, the plan has no room for a January 2027 cutover, and any slippage in the HCM/payroll parallel runs pushes the contractual go-live date. The bidder risks a schedule it cannot contract to and a scored criterion it cannot satisfy as written. The two requirements are directly contradictory and the January 1, 2027 date is also a scored evaluation criterion, so the conflict is certain to surface; a full financials-plus-HCM-plus-payroll rollout in roughly 22 months leaves no float.
items.reason: Sources show March 2025–January 2027 and go-live by January 1, 2027; 'directly contradictory' overstated, and HCM/payroll parallel runs, 22 months, and scope not cited.

items.text: Scope baseline sits in a separate Requirements document not in the RFP. The module list and functionality are defined only by reference to a separate ERP Requirements document and a Section 6 template, neither of which is in the RFP text. If those documents contain modules, interfaces or functions beyond the eleven named modules, the fixed implementation price and the 22-month plan are both understated. The bidder carries the risk of a scope it has not seen. The RFP's own scope section defers to the Requirements document, and the solution explicitly assumes that document is the definitive and complete baseline; the bid is priced before that assumption can be tested.
items.reason: Deferral to Requirements document is supported; 'eleven named modules', fixed price, 22-month plan, and solution assumption are not in cited sources.

items.text: Current-environment and in-scope-solutions tables missing. The RFP refers to tables describing the City's current environment and which existing solutions are in scope for replacement, but those tables are not in the document. Without them the bidder cannot know how many legacy systems must be interfaced or retired, how much data conversion is needed, or whether third-party systems outside the ERP must be replaced. Data conversion and integration are the most common source of overrun on ERP implementations. The solution assumes the tables cover only the named modules and prices no additional legacy replacement; that assumption is untested and conversion/integration effort scales directly with the number of source systems.
items.reason: Scope tables referenced but not included in S6.1; data conversion and integration requirements are stated. Assumption about solution is a position.

items.text: Demo Script not available at bid time. Finalists must demo strictly to a City-issued Demo Script, but the script is only issued with the demo notification and is not in the RFP. The bidder must prepare a December 2024 on-site demo without knowing which functions will be scripted, and demo performance feeds the Software and Implementation scores. A demo that misses scripted items costs evaluation points the written proposal cannot recover. The script is confirmed as a separate document issued later, and the solution assumes preparation is scoped from it; the demo is a scored gate in December 2024.
items.reason: Script-based demos, December 2024, and Demo Script issued with notification are supported; 'on-site' demo and the claim that demo scores feed Software and Implementation criteria are not stated.

items.text: Pricing template ambiguities drive rework and price risk. Exhibit A is not in the RFP, the template lists Project and Grant Accounting twice, and it does not say whether Year 1 software is a perpetual licence or a subscription or how Years 2-10 maintenance relates to it. The bidder must guess the pricing structure for a ten-year commitment, and a misread structure can make the bid non-comparable or misprice the maintenance tail. The solution explicitly assumes the duplicate line is one module and that Year 1 is a subscription with Years 2-10 as annual subscription lines; both are inferences the RFP does not settle, and maintenance over ten years dominates lifecycle cost.
items.reason: Duplicate Project and Grant Accounting and Years 2-10 maintenance are supported; 'Exhibit A is not in the RFP' contradicts S12.1, which shows it.

The page is confirmed unreadable, but whether it matters depends on its content, which the bid team cannot see from the extracted text.

items.text: Insurance requirements unpriced and unquantified. The RFP requires a certificate of insurance with an underwriter's endorsement naming the City as additional insured and a surety admitted in Washington, but names no coverage types, limits or additional insured parties. The bidder must price coverage it cannot size, and a certificate that does not match the City's unstated expectations can delay contract execution or block work from starting. The obligation is mandatory and precedes any work, while the solution assumes standard commercial general liability, professional liability, cyber and workers' compensation at customary limits — an assumption the RFP does not confirm.
items.reason: Certificate, endorsement, and admitted surety supported; 'naming the City as additional insured' and no limits stated are not explicit, and cited sources do not show coverage types.

items.text: Deployment options and best-of-breed HCM left open. The RFP requires a separate pricing sheet per deployment option but does not say whether both SaaS and on-premises must be priced, and it does not say whether a best-of-breed HCM bid may stand alone or must be paired with an ERP. The solution prices SaaS as primary with on-premises as a secondary sheet and offers best-of-breed HCM only as an alternative, so a different City reading means missing or mispriced sheets and a lower Software score. Both points are unresolved in the RFP and the solution resolves them by assumption; the Software criterion is worth 30 points and the pricing sheets are mandatory submission items.
items.reason: Pricing sheet per deployment option, best-of-breed HCM integration, 30-point Software criterion all stated; remaining content is solution position and judgment.}

items.text: Requirements document completion effort and rating rules. Every line of the City's Requirements document must carry a rating on the 4/3/2/0/F scale plus a comment of no more than 100 words, with no blank cells, no hyperlinks and no format changes, and items rated 3, 2 or F carry extra obligations (third-party name, modification cost, release date). The RFP does not settle whether a rating of 0 needs a comment or whether the word limit covers the whole cell. With a large requirement set this is a substantial, easily underestimated effort, and a blank or malformed cell can cause rejection as incomplete. The obligation is mandatory and rejection is an explicit consequence of blank responses, while the rating and word-limit rules are ambiguous; the effort scales with a requirement count the bidder has not yet seen.
items.reason: Rating scale, 100-word limit, no hyperlinks, format rules, extra obligations, and blank-response rejection are all stated in sources.

items.text: Phased rollout assumption may not match City approval. The solution assumes a phased rollout with financials live ahead of HCM and payroll, subject to City approval at mobilisation. The RFP leaves the approach open and states no approval criteria, so the City could require a different phasing or a single big-bang cutover, which would change the design, the staffing plan and the price after contract signature. The RFP permits either a phased or a vendor-recommended approach approved by the City but gives no criteria, and the solution's phasing is an inference rather than a confirmed requirement.
items.reason: Phased or vendor-recommended approach approved by City, no criteria stated; staffing and methodology are evaluation criteria.

items.text: Reference requirements may not be met as defined. The RFP requires three current and two prior customer references on Exhibit B forms, with preference for Washington State public sector clients of comparable size and scope, but does not define what makes a reference current or comparable. If the bidder cannot produce five qualifying references, the Vendor criterion (15 points) is weakened and the submission may be judged incomplete. The reference count is mandatory and the comparability criteria are undefined; the solution assumes three current and two prior customers live on the proposed software, comparable on employee count and module scope, which the RFP does not confirm.
